description:
Under `--json` a propagated failure renders once, as the stdout envelope, instead of also printing an `Error:` line to stderr.

## Background

`main()` in `crates/jit/src/main.rs` handles `run()`'s error with `eprintln!("Error: {}", e)` unconditionally and then calls `emit_top_level_json_error`, so every propagated failure under `--json` prints both a stderr diagnostic and the stdout envelope (reproduced with `jit apply plan <id> --json`). Handler-owned failures already leave stderr empty. `test_propagated_config_parse_failure_emits_registered_envelope_and_human_diagnostic` in `crates/jit/tests/cli_issue/top_level_failure_envelope_tests.rs` asserts the duplicate stderr line, and `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` says errors are "always shown to stderr". With `--json` declared once as a global flag, the parsed output mode reaches `main()` beside `run()`'s result, so `main()` can choose one rendering.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Once clap has accepted the arguments, a failing invocation with `--json` writes exactly one failure envelope to stdout and nothing to stderr, for propagated and handler-owned failures alike.
- [hard] REQ-02: A failing invocation without `--json` writes one `Error:` diagnostic to stderr and nothing to stdout.
- [hard] REQ-03: The propagated-failure test in `top_level_failure_envelope_tests.rs` states the new contract (empty stderr under `--json`), and a human-mode test owns the single-diagnostic property.
- [hard] REQ-04: The "always shown to stderr" statement in `docs/reference/cli-commands.md` describes the new behaviour.
- [hard] REQ-05: `main()` chooses the rendering from the parsed output mode; no raw-argv scan decides it.

## Notes

Clap parse failures stay outside the envelope and keep writing to stderr. Success-path warnings, such as those `issue create` prints, stay on stderr as documented; this change concerns failure rendering only. Design rationale: `dev/active/df129d9e-rust-code-quality/plan.md`.
title: Keep stderr empty for --json failures
